title: Workers at 15% CPU but the queue keeps growing — what gives?

posts.author: scale_sarah
posts.body: Pushing ~30k jobs/sec. We have 6 worker hosts, `workers.concurrency: 32` each. CPU on the workers sits around 15%, but `corvex_queue_depth` climbs all day. Adding more workers doesn't help. Jobs themselves are fast (~5ms, mostly an HTTP call). Where's the bottleneck?

posts.author: redis_ron
posts.body:
Classic connection-pool starvation. Every busy job slot holds one Redis connection. You have 6 × 32 = 192 slots per host but `storage.redis.pool_size` defaults to 10, so 182 slots are constantly parked waiting for a connection — that's why CPU is low and more workers make it worse (more contention, same pool). Check `corvex_storage_pool_wait_seconds`; I bet p50 is well above zero.

Set `storage.redis.pool_size` to at least `concurrency + 4` (so ~36), make sure your Redis `maxclients` and the OS file-descriptor limit can take 6 × 36 connections, and also switch to batch enqueue (`POST /api/v1/jobs:batch`) if you're enqueuing one at a time.

posts.author: scale_sarah
posts.body: `pool_size: 40` and the queue drained in minutes. `pool_wait_seconds` p50 was 0.8s before, ~0 now. Thank you.
